## Archery at the 2012 Summer Olympics — Women’s team

The **women’s team archery** event at the **2012 Summer Olympics in London** was a recurve archery team competition held at **Lord’s Cricket Ground**, one of the most distinctive venues of the Games.

### Basic details

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Event | Women’s team recurve archery |
| Games | 2012 Summer Olympics, London |
| Venue | Lord’s Cricket Ground, London |
| Dates | Ranking round: 27 July 2012; elimination/finals: 29 July 2012 |
| Teams | 12 national teams |
| Archers per team | 3 |
| Distance | 70 metres |
| Gold medal | South Korea |
| Silver medal | China |
| Bronze medal | Japan |

---

## Medalists

### Gold — South Korea  
**Ki Bo-bae, Lee Sung-jin, Choi Hyeon-ju**

South Korea continued its extraordinary Olympic dominance in women’s team archery. The Korean women had won every Olympic women’s team title since the event was introduced in 1988, and London 2012 extended that streak.

### Silver — China  
**Cheng Ming, Fang Yuting, Xu Jing**

China pushed South Korea extremely close in the final, losing by only one point.

### Bronze — Japan  
**Kaori Kawanaka, Ren Hayakawa, Miki Kanie**

Japan defeated Russia in the bronze-medal match to win its first Olympic medal in the women’s team archery event.

---

## Final result

### Gold-medal match  
**South Korea defeated China, 210–209**

This was a very close final. South Korea won by a single point, preserving its perfect Olympic record in the women’s team event.

### Bronze-medal match  
**Japan defeated Russia, 209–207**

Japan earned the bronze medal with a two-point win over Russia.

---

## Competition format

The event used the standard Olympic recurve team format of the time.

### Ranking round
Each archer shot **72 arrows** at 70 metres.  
The three individual scores from each country were added together to produce the team’s ranking-round score.

Those team scores determined the seedings for the knockout bracket.

### Elimination matches
Each team match consisted of **24 arrows per team**:

- 3 archers per team
- Each archer shot 8 arrows total
- Teams alternated shooting
- The team with the higher cumulative score advanced

Unlike later Olympic archery formats, the 2012 team event used **total-score matchplay**, not the modern set system.

---

## Participating teams

Twelve women’s teams competed:

- China
- Chinese Taipei
- Denmark
- Great Britain
- India
- Italy
- Japan
- Mexico
- Russia
- South Korea
- Ukraine
- United States

---

## Podium significance

South Korea’s victory was historically important because it extended the country’s unbeaten Olympic streak in the women’s team event.

The women’s team event was introduced at the **1988 Seoul Olympics**, and South Korea won gold in:

- 1988 Seoul
- 1992 Barcelona
- 1996 Atlanta
- 2000 Sydney
- 2004 Athens
- 2008 Beijing
- 2012 London

So, London 2012 marked South Korea’s **seventh consecutive Olympic gold medal** in the women’s team archery event.

---

## South Korea’s team

### Ki Bo-bae
Ki Bo-bae was one of the stars of the London archery competition. In addition to the team gold, she also went on to win the **individual women’s gold medal**, making her a double Olympic champion in London.

### Lee Sung-jin
Lee Sung-jin was an experienced Korean archer who had already won Olympic medals before 2012, including team gold in 2004 and individual silver in 2004.

### Choi Hyeon-ju
Choi Hyeon-ju completed the Korean trio and contributed to the team’s narrow win over China in the final.

---

## China’s team

China’s silver-medal team consisted of:

- Cheng Ming
- Fang Yuting
- Xu Jing

China had also been South Korea’s main challenger in women’s team archery at the previous Olympics. At Beijing 2008, China also won silver behind South Korea.

---

## Japan’s team

Japan’s bronze-medal team consisted of:

- Kaori Kawanaka
- Ren Hayakawa
- Miki Kanie

Their bronze medal was a major result for Japanese archery and one of the highlights of Japan’s archery performance at the London Games.

---

## Final standings

| Rank | Country |
|---:|---|
| 1 | South Korea |
| 2 | China |
| 3 | Japan |
| 4 | Russia |
| 5–8 | Quarter-final losers |
| 9–12 | First-round losers |

The official medal standings were:

1. **South Korea**
2. **China**
3. **Japan**

---

## Venue: Lord’s Cricket Ground

Archery at London 2012 was held at **Lord’s**, one of the most famous cricket grounds in the world. Temporary archery ranges and spectator stands were installed for the Olympics. The setting was widely praised because it combined a traditional British sporting venue with a very different Olympic sport.

---

## Notable facts

- South Korea won the event by only **one point** in the final.
- The gold medal continued South Korea’s perfect Olympic record in women’s team archery.
- Ki Bo-bae won both the **team** and **individual** women’s archery gold medals at London 2012.
- Japan’s bronze was its first Olympic medal in the women’s team event.
- The competition used cumulative scoring rather than the set-based format used in later Olympic archery events.
